title: 90-Minute Feature Film Made Entirely by AI Airs on Three Satellite TV Stations: Shenzhen's First AIGC Feature-Length Film "Wonderful Connection" Uses No Live-Action Camera

content_html:
A roughly 90-minute feature-length narrative film contains no traditional live-action shooting from start to finish, yet it delivers a delicate and vivid live-action visual texture—on November 23, Shenzhen's first AIGC (generative artificial intelligence) online narrative film, "Wonderful Connection," premiered simultaneously on Shenzhen TV, Hunan TV, and Mango TV, pushing AI video technology to the full specifications of a feature-length online narrative film for the first time.

The story is set against the backdrop of China's APEC year in 2026. Starting with an urban adventure triggered by an email, the film tells of the wondrous encounters in Shenzhen between an ordinary employee of a Shenzhen company and four overseas clients from South Korea, Mexico, Indonesia, and Chile. Characters from different cultural backgrounds and professional identities communicate and come to understand one another through a series of experiences full of laughter and warmth, ultimately forming a sincere emotional bond between people, folding the grand proposition of jointly building an Asia-Pacific community into a tangible, relatable screen story. The brisk pace of workplace comedy and the humanistic concern of realism are stitched into the same narrative thread.

The city itself is also one of the film's protagonists. In the early stages, the creative team went deep into Shenzhen to gather material, conducting field research on landmark buildings, industrial parks, streets, and neighborhoods. They turned a large amount of the real city's scenery into digital assets, then used AI to recreate an authentic and vibrant urban texture—Shenzhen's technological innovation strength, industrial vitality, and urban warmth flow naturally along with the characters' experiences, portraying the city's most modern and dynamic side.

Unlike many traditional AIGC works that are eager to show off technical tricks, this film's production approach reverses the order: the creative logic of live-action filmmaking and a complete scripted narrative framework come first, with AI tools serving the storytelling rather than the other way around. From script planning, character design, and the construction of digital scene assets to video generation, shot composition, lighting, and art direction, the core creative work was completed by the creative team of Shenzhen Sunshine Pictures. It was co-produced by Shenzhen Sunshine Pictures, Shenzhen Film Studio Co., Ltd., and other units, with guidance and support from the Publicity Department of the CPC Shenzhen Municipal Committee. When a film without cameras can achieve cinematic audiovisual aesthetics and appear on mainstream satellite TV screens, the path of AIGC film and television from technology demonstration to serious content production has been made one step more solid.
